title: Number of Ways to Split Array
statement:
You get an integer array `nums` of length `n`. Cutting it after index `i` (where `0 <= i < n - 1`, so both parts are non-empty) produces a left part `nums[0..i]` and a right part `nums[i+1..n-1]`. The cut is valid when the left part's sum is at least the right part's sum.

Return the number of indices `i` that give a valid cut.
notes:
## Intuition

Recomputing both part sums for every cut costs O(n) per cut and O(n²) overall. But moving the cut one step right only moves one element, `nums[i]`, from the right part to the left part. So keep a running prefix sum for the left part, and get the right part as `total - leftSum`, since the two parts always add up to the whole array.

## Approach

1. Add up the whole array into `total`.
2. Walk `i` from `0` to `n - 2` (the last element can never be the end of the left part, because the right part must be non-empty).
3. Add `nums[i]` to `leftSum` and set `rightSum = total - leftSum`.
4. If `leftSum >= rightSum`, count the cut in `ways`.
5. Return `ways`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [10, 4, -8, 7]`, `total = 13`.

| `i` | `leftSum` | `rightSum` | valid? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 10 | 3 | yes |
| 1 | 14 | -1 | yes |
| 2 | 6 | 7 | no |

So `ways = 2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass for `total`, one pass for the cuts.
- Space: O(1): only a few running numbers.

## Pitfalls

- Stop at `n - 2`; cutting after the last element leaves an empty right part, which is not allowed.
- The comparison is `>=`, so equal sums count as valid.
- Sums can reach about `10^10`, beyond a 32-bit int; in Java or C keep `total` and `leftSum` in a 64-bit type.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `total` | sum of the whole array |
| `value` | each element while summing `total` |
| `leftSum` | sum of `nums[0..i]` |
| `rightSum` | sum of `nums[i+1..n-1]`, found as `total - leftSum` |
| `ways` | number of valid cuts so far |
| `i` | the last index of the left part |

narration.2: total will hold the sum of the whole array.
narration.3: Visit every element once to add it in.
narration.7: leftSum is the running sum of the left part; it starts empty.
narration.9: Try every cut that leaves at least one element on the right, so i stops at n - 2.
narration.10: Moving the cut right shifts nums[i] into the left part.
narration.11: The right part is everything not in the left part.
narration.12: The cut is valid when the left part's sum is at least the right part's.
narration.16: Return how many cuts were valid.
